texts.li: [winter] {X_nameDef} has been carrying the {FACTION} party's loads through the snow with rags for gloves. Tonight {X_nameDef} found {A_nameDef} alone in the storeroom and asked, shaking, to be hidden when the others leave.\n\n{FACTION} counts {X_nameDef} as theirs, and will remember who kept {X_objective}.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} wears the iron collar of a {FACTION} bondservant, and came to {A_nameDef} at the well to ask if it's true that this colony takes people in. {X_nameDef} wants to stay when the {FACTION} party moves on.\n\nThe {FACTION} elders won't take it kindly.

[winter] {X_nameDef} has asked the wardens for a second blanket, a hot meal at noon, and a date for the release, in that order. Word on the road is that the colony lets its prisoners go, and {X_nameDef} is planning around it, down to the day.

[winter] {FACTION} are going hungry this winter, and the colony's name on their roads is a hard one. {A_nameDef} heard a trader say so at the gate, and has asked the council to send them food, once, and ask nothing for it.

[theirLowtech] The {FACTION} elders have brought {X_nameDef} into the yard with {X_possessive} hands bound, caught stealing from their own carts. In their villages, they say, a thief is beaten by a stranger so no family carries the feud. They've heard this colony doesn't flinch, and have asked for {A_nameDef}.

[winter] The cold has brought {FACTION}'s hungry to the gate every morning, and {A_nameDef} has fed all of them out of the colony's stores. The only tracks in the snow run from the road to the gate.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council how much more can go out before spring.

[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} hasn't turned anyone from {FACTION} away from the gate all season, and doesn't want to start. But the storeroom is thinner than it should be, and {A_nameDef} has brought the count to the council, hating every number on it.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has started a tab for the colony's goods "since you lot like counting," and reads it aloud every time {A_nameDef} passes. The caravan guards think it's the funniest thing they've heard all season.\n\n{A_nameDef} has stopped passing.

[winter] On the longest night the colony keeps a candle burning in every window until dawn, as it always has. {A_nameDef} put {A_possessive} out to save the wax, and said so. {B_nameDef} saw, and has brought it to the council.

[spring] At the first planting the colony always walks the fields together before anyone picks up a hoe. {A_nameDef} skipped the walk and started work early, and {B_nameDef} has asked the council to remind {A_objective} what the custom is for.

[winter] There used to be a night each winter when the colony told the story of its first year, around one fire, with every last person there. It stopped somewhere along the way, and no one can say which winter. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to bring it back this year, and keep it.

[winter] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has taken the chair closest to the stove for three days running, and won't give it up even when {A_nameDef} comes in frozen from the fields. Last night {A_nameDef} ate supper standing by the door, still in {A_possessive} coat.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} visitors, is camped outside the walls in the snow, because the colony lets no stranger in after dark. {X_nameDef} is the friend {A_nameDef} talks about from before. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to open the gate tonight, just once.

[summer] It's the height of summer and the colony is working through it, as it always does. {A_nameDef} fainted in the field this afternoon from the heat and the hours, and has asked the council, once {A_pronoun} could stand, for a day off.

[fall] The harvest is in, and {A_nameDef} brought most of it in alone while the others found reasons to be somewhere else. {A_nameDef} has come to the council with blistered hands and a short speech about it.
